items.title: feat(aggregator): Refresh quota button (generatedAt polling) + -direct display-name rule (#6125)
items.body: Two deliverables from #6125 (Drew 2026-11-05 01:25 CST) for the LVIS/pm-aggregator dashboard. ## 1. Refresh quota button The quota surface had a bare `Refresh now` form (#1171) with no client feedback. Now: - Button labeled **Refresh quota** POSTs the manual trigger via the existing `POST /api/quota/refresh` route (`quotaRefresher.manual` -> `quota-gatherer.service`; the gatherer is the single quota source). No new route needed; the route response now also returns the baseline `generatedAt`. - Shows a refreshing state and polls `/api/quota.json` every 5s (up to the gatherer 6-min bound) until `quota-current.json` **generatedAt advances**, then reloads to display the new data. - No faked success: gatherer-reported failure (`gatherer.ok === false`), a failed request, or no advance within the window all render an explicit failure message and re-enable the button. - No-JS form fallback (`POST /quota/refresh`, same manual trigger) retained; the strip also now renders on the no-usage quota layout. ## 2. `-direct` display-name rule (markup only) New pure function `providerDisplayNames` / `providerDisplayName` in `src/provider-display.ts`, computed over the actual rendered provider set (never hardcoded): strip a trailing `-direct` iff no non-direct provider with the same base name exists in the same set. Dotted pool ids judge by their provider head segment (`antigravity-direct.gemini` -> `antigravity.gemini` on the real set); ids/keys/hrefs are never rewritten. Applied in `renderQuota` (pool providers, burn rows, model-choice pool lists, credential-lifecycle names), the Today walled-pools banner, and the overview quota strip. ## Tests - New `test/provider-display.test.ts`: strip-when-base-absent, keep-when-base-present, per-set decision, non-direct untouched, dotted ids, map-key/id stability, plus render integration for the rule and the button markup/polling/failure copy. - `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean. - Full suite: 1465 pass / 19 fail vs unmodified main baseline 1455 pass / 19 fail (same 19 pre-existing failures, verified on main; +10 new tests all pass). Refs #6125 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: quota: gatherer reads only the opencode quota subcommand + Supabase sink (#6127)
items.body: Single-source quota rewire — program #6125, closes the gatherer half of #6127 once the fork subcommand (developing-today-forks/opencode#1718) is deployed to the tick. **What changes** - The tick's only quota read is now the opencode quota subcommand: `opencode quota --json` (configured listing) + `opencode quota --json meta command-code` (explicit ask for route-disabled live pools; a named ask always fetches). Results map through the unchanged quota-gather-map contract. - Retired from the gatherer: in-process OpenChamber module import, gatherer-side Turso read, native ClinePass adapter fill, file-export family, Claude expiry side-read (subcommand results carry credentialExpiresAt/credentialSource). - Kept: OpenDesign session keeper (credential maintenance, runs before the read; its store accessors still resolve from the OpenChamber lib — plumbing, not a reading path), #1268 retention, #1331 pool splits, Command Code plan-window mapping, fail-soft heartbeat (a broken subcommand leaves the previous quota-current.json standing). - `quota-current.json` source becomes `opencode-quota` (GATHERER_SOURCE) — the file names its real producer. - **Supabase sink added:** one `agent.quota_records` row per pool entry per tick, source `opencode-quota`, pm-pool payload shape. The previous pool writer (source `pm-pool`) died 2026-10-29 — verified in muse-dev2: 12 rows ever, none since. Fail-soft after the file write. - README gatherer section rewritten to match. **Verification so far:** `bunx tsc --noEmit` clean; quota test files (quota-gather-map, quota-current, credential-lifecycle) 106 pass / 0 fail. Live tick against the fork-built subcommand binary + the production drop-in flip land with opencode#1718's proof on #6125 — this PR merges in the same motion as that deployment so the timer never runs the new gatherer against a binary without the subcommand. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: quota: run the subcommand from a neutral cwd (state dir)
items.body: Follow-up to #6136 (program #6125, issue #6127). The first production tick of the rewired gatherer failed: launched by systemd from the aggregator's repo cwd, the opencode CLI did project discovery over the code repo's worktree forest — 6m13s CPU, the 240s exec cap truncated the listing stdout, and the tick failed loudly (fail-soft held; the previous quota-current.json stood). Quota is a machine-level read, not a project read: the gatherer now execs the subcommand with cwd = the aggregator state dir. Proven production-style (unit's cwd + env, worktree script): full tick in 58s, 14 providers / 12 ok, mistral single ok row, Supabase sink 16 rows. Also: the unparseable-output error now carries the byte count. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: quota: default OPENCODE_CONFIG_PATH for subcommand execs
items.body: Follow-up to #6136/#6190 (program #6125, issue #6127). The neutral-cwd fix was not sufficient under the real unit: interactive shells on the laptop carry OPENCODE_CONFIG_PATH (the standing runtime config), the systemd unit does not — and without it the CLI's default config discovery takes minutes even from a neutral cwd (240s cap, truncated stdout; evidence on opencode#1729). With the variable set, the same binary under systemd completes the listing in ~37s. The gatherer now defaults OPENCODE_CONFIG_PATH for its subcommand execs to the standing runtime config file, respecting an explicitly set value. Proven via a transient systemd unit with the unit's sparse env: full tick RC=0, quota-current.json regenerated (source opencode-quota, mistral ok with both dollar budgets). --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * The quota command now uses the configured OpenCode config path when available. If none is set, it uses the default runtime config path.

items.title: fix(mcpx): hold the artifact name claim across the delivery write (#4253)
items.body: Fixes the never-overwrite race triaged in #4253 (task 6125, confirmed on main; fix = task 6127). **The bug:** `uniquePath` created its O_EXCL claim file, deleted it, and returned the bare path. `Store.Export` (via `copyInto`), the exec streaming path, and `fetchArtifacts` (via `writeNew`) then finished with an overwriting `os.Rename` onto that path — a destination appearing in the window was silently replaced, and two concurrent same-name deliveries could both be handed the same path. **The fix:** `ClaimPath` (replacing the racy `UniquePath` API) returns the destination already created, with the O_EXCL claim held open. Every delivery path writes into the claim and closes it; on failure the claimed name is removed, so nothing partial looks delivered. Writing into the claim is a copy, per the #1660 settlement — no link semantics introduced. **Tests** (failing-first, class-wide per `internal/AGENTS.md`): - `TestClaimPathHoldsTheNameUntilTheWriteIsDone` — the exact interleaving: a second claim while the first write is in flight gets the suffixed name. - `TestExportConcurrentSameNameDeliveriesAllSurvive` — 8 concurrent same-name exports, distinct paths, own bytes. - `TestExportKeepsAForeignFileThatHoldsTheName` / `TestFetchArtifactsKeepsAForeignFileThatHoldsTheName` — foreign bytes preserved, delivery suffixes, recorded Path matches the file written. - `TestDeliveryPathsHoldTheirClaims` — source guard: no `UniquePath` references remain; the CLI delivery file must not rename onto a destination again. CI-first: targeted package tests were not run locally (laptop under extreme load); CI results on this PR are the verification. Parked in the queue awaiting CI + Codex review. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.
